incidents.summary: Barratt Redrow and other housebuilders accepted commitments including a combined £100 million affordable-housing contribution following competition concerns, and subsequently faced a class action alleging price-inflating collusion extending back to 2015.

sources.title: UK housebuilders face class action suit over alleged collusion to inflate prices | Construction industry | The Guardian
sources.quote: Britain’s biggest housebuilders, including Barratt Redrow and Taylor Wimpey, face a multibillion-pound class action lawsuit over claims that they colluded over higher prices for homebuyers.

sources.title: Class action lawyers target UK housebuilders | Estates Gazette
sources.quote: The companies accepted binding commitments in October last year to address the regulator’s concerns, including a pledge not to share commercially sensitive information in future and a £100m contribution to affordable housing.

sources.title: Class action lawyers target UK housebuilders | Estates Gazette
sources.quote: Hausfeld said this claim goes further than the CMA’s findings, alleging the information sharing extended back to October 2015.

incidents.summary: Concrete-frame defects were discovered at Citiscape and other Barratt developments, with the group's reported total bill for building-safety defects reaching £1,073.8 million in September 2025.

sources.title: Barratt Redrow
sources.quote: In 2020, during remedial work to replace flammable cladding at the Citiscape high-rise in Croydon, defects were found in the reinforced concrete frame of the building.

sources.title: Barratt Redrow
sources.quote: Citiscape residents were rehoused in September 2019, and in May 2021, Barratt reacquired the 95 flats at Citiscape from their leaseholders

sources.title: Barratt Redrow
sources.quote: In September 2025, the group's total bill to fix building safety defects was £1,073.8m, a figure which was virtually unchanged a year later.

incidents.summary: Barratt submitted plans to demolish 83 new homes at its Darwin Green estate in Cambridge because they had faulty foundations.

sources.title: Barratt Redrow
sources.quote: In September 2023, Barratt submitted plans to demolish 83 new homes on its Darwin Green estate in Cambridge which had been built with faulty foundations.

incidents.summary: Barratt Redrow subsidiary BDW Trading admitted responsibility for silt pollution of two Yate watercourses and agreed a £201,500 environmental payment after spending more than £180,000 on remediation, training and improved practices.

sources.title: Builder pays £201,500 to charities after silting watercourses - GOV.UK
sources.quote: BDW Trading, part of the Barratt Redrow group, polluted the Ladden Brook and Tanhouse stream in Yate over six days in July 2022.

sources.title: Housebuilder pays £201,500 after silt pollutes watercourses - Water Magazine
sources.quote: BDW Trading, part of Barratt Redrow, has agreed a £201,500 environmental payment after silt from a Yate housing development polluted two watercourses.

sources.title: Housebuilder pays £201,500 after silt pollutes watercourses - Water Magazine
sources.quote: BDW Trading acknowledged responsibility and subsequently spent more than £180,000 on remediation, staff training and improved practices for managing surface water.

positives: The completed £3.5 million Conningbrook Wetland at Redrow's Crown Hill View development delivers nutrient neutrality through an on-site mitigation scheme.
